Under the European Commission's EU AI Act guidelines, providers of open-source general-purpose AI models are exempted from the following obligations:

1. The obligation to draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model (Article 53(1), point (a)).
2. The obligation to draw up, keep up-to-date, and make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the general-purpose AI model into their AI systems (Article 53(1), point (b)).
3. The obligation to appoint an authorised representative for providers of general-purpose AI models established in third countries (Article 54 AI Act).

However, they must still fulfil the following obligations:

1. The obligation to put in place a policy to comply with Union copyright law (Article 53(1), point (c)).
2. The obligation to produce a summary about the content used for training (Article 53(1), point (d)). 

These exemptions apply as long as the model is not classified as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk.
